correctness.rationale: For every integer length 31..64 a literal ternary last column is supplied. The exact rank-stable permutation is a single n-cycle, the last column has no equal adjacent symbols, and the Hamming distance to its sorted rearrangement is ceil(n/2). Both verifier programs were executed successfully on all 34 rows; the independent inversion program reconstructs primitive necklaces and their BWT by directly sorting all rotations and counts cyclic runs. The published factor-two theorem supplies the universal lower bound. The at-most-six-third-letter property is checked explicitly.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 primary article leaves all-length sharpness as a conjecture and supplies examples through 12 and arithmetic families. Previously recoverable local enumeration through length 30 is outside this claim. Six specific lengths within 31..64 already follow from the cited prime-root theorem; the other 28 are newly certified by supplied explicit last columns. The 2025 complete-unclustering existence result does not control the minimum input-run count. Several actual literature/record searches returned no comparable interval-wide sharpness theorem; priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The open and specifically named sharpness conjecture motivates verifying a contiguous block, rather than arbitrary word statistics. The 34 cases extend the recovered certificate frontier from length 30 to the natural dyadic bound 64, closing 28 cases not implied by the published prime-root family. Every new witness uses at most six insertions of the third symbol into a binary alternating last column, providing additional structural information relevant to possible sparse constructive families. This is a meaningful finite cutoff, not a general proof.
